description: ABSTAIN FROM MINTING AT A MARKED CUT (VISION_CUT_MINT_POLICY_PREREG.md, seeds 75000-75999). THE DEFECT THIS ADDRESSES IS THE INCUMBENT'S OWN DECOMPOSITION: VISION_VIDEO_ACCUMULATION_RESULTS.md section 3.2 measured that MDL tile-selection is worth +0.0625 (C1) / +0.0475 (C2) with the frame distribution HELD FIXED -- CI-separated on both corpora, the mechanism works everywhere -- while drawing from the system's OWN cut-concentrated frame distribution COSTS -0.0265 / -0.0420, also CI-separated on both. `When it mints is a liability; which tile it picks is the asset.` So the fix is not a better selector; it is to STOP MINTING AT CUTS. ONE RULE, AND IT IS THE DECISION. `cm_abstain_mint` fires on an Observation the seam has already declared `is_novel` -- so the seam's own measured-noise-floor verdict has had its full say and the graph still holds what it WOULD have minted -- and, if a FrameStep INCIDENT ON THAT OBSERVATION'S FRAME carries the `is_cut` mark another rule wrote, it declines: status becomes `cm_abstained`, so `is_mint` (which requires `is_novel`) never matches, and no ShapeSignature is added. NOTHING HERE IS A PYTHON CONDITIONAL: the adapter draws one `at_step` edge from each Observation to the (at most two) steps incident on the frame the runner just presented -- an interval the runner already constructed, exactly the `spans` precedent of vision_cut_abstention -- and then stops. THE CUT MARK IS NOT THIS SEED'S: it is `seeds/vision_cut_abstention.json`, LOADED UNEDITED, whose `ca_step_mag` / `ca_otsu` / `ca_mark_cut` derive a threshold from the sequence's own distribution with NO free parameter and no numeric literal anywhere (protocol section 13, gated in that rung). THE WINDOW IS NOT A PARAMETER, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. A frame abstains iff a step INCIDENT on it is marked -- the step into it or the step out of it. The seam rung's inherited W=3 window would have caught 16 (C1) / 10 (C2) of the incumbent's mints instead of 6 / 6, making the predicted effect 2.7x / 1.7x larger; W is a magic number and choosing it after computing that fraction would be metric surgery (protocol sections 5 and 13). The small fraction is reported as the cost of the discipline, not designed around. RULE ORDER IS LOAD ORDER AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING: `run_rules` iterates the rule vector in install order and restarts at index 0 on progress, so a rule that must pre-empt `is_mint` has to be INSTALLED BEFORE IT. `domains/cut_mint_world.py` therefore loads this manifest before `vision_identity_seam`, and two gates hold that honest -- the installed order is asserted, and with this seed DISARMED the grown codebook is byte-identical to the incumbent AccumWorld's (same K, same mints, same frames and regions). THE ABSTENTION LEAVES A TRACE, following the cut-abstention rung's finding that an abstention no reader can see is indistinguishable from a healthy run: a MintAbstention node is minted (add_node_if_absent, so exactly one per observation and the fixpoint terminates), a `mint_abstained_by` edge is drawn, and `mint_abstained` is set on the observation. SHIPS DISARMED (CutMintParams.armed = 0.0) and is NOT in the default boot set -- the runner loads this manifest explicitly and arms it, so the disarmed configuration reproduces every committed accumulation number (protocol section 9).

rules.name: cm_abstain_mint
rules.comment: THE POLICY, AND IT IS THE GRAPH'S DECISION. An observation the seam has judged novel (is_decide wrote `is_novel` because its best NCC did not clear the MEASURED noise floor) whose own frame is incident on a step marked `is_cut` has had its frame-to-frame prior broken at exactly the moment it would have minted, so the system declines to add it to the codebook. `identified_as` is deliberately LEFT INTACT (is_decide wrote `novel` there) so the graph still holds what it would have done and the cost of the abstention stays measurable -- the same discipline ca_abstain used. The status write is what does the work: `is_mint` requires status == `is_novel`, so `cm_abstained` pre-empts it without this seed touching, reading or editing the seam's rule. The armed guard is a Count over CutMintParams with armed > 0.5, matching the seam's own arming idiom, so the seed is inert until a measurement arms it (protocol section 9). Note what is NOT here: no motion magnitude, no threshold, no window and no numeric literal outside {0.5, 1, 0} -- 0.5 is the seam's own arming midpoint idiom, 1 is the is_cut flag another rule set, 0 is a count. The cut decision was made by ca_mark_cut against a threshold ca_otsu derived from the data; this rule only reads the flag.
